720	The head knows what is right and wrong,
721	right? For example, a person about to commit a transgression
722	usually knows he is about to commit a transgression. That is
723	why he looks right and left. Why? Because the mind
724	knows it is not good. But why does he commit
725	the transgression? Because the heart desires. The heart has desire.
726	So if you are a king, the mind rules the heart, then the mind
727	defeats the heart. But if you are Lemech, first comes desire,
728	and only after that the intellect, then you are like the nations. So what does He
729	tell him? "And He will give their kings into your hand": whatever you would call
730	their way, which is the way of Lemech, will be yours,
731	you will rule over it. Another point:
732	Why does He give the kings? So that you know that if
733	the king falls,
734	the whole people falls after him. Right? How did he make
735	his minister fall in heaven? The moment Moshe Rabbeinu saw the minister
736	of Og thrown down to the floor, he understood that they were already
737	losing. The moment one is cast down from heaven to the ground, the whole
738	people will lose. Same thing here on earth. The people see the
739	king fall, everyone surrenders, they do not fight. How do
740	we know? In Yehoshua it is written: "And they brought out those kings
741	to Yehoshua." They won, they brought the kings
742	to Yehoshua. "And Yehoshua called all the men of Israel and said
743	to the commanders of the men of war who went with him: Come near, put your
744	feet on the necks of these kings." They made the
745	kings lie down, and all the commanders of Israel put their
746	foot on their throats, which is the sign of humiliation and submission,
747	and it was fulfilled exactly as it is written here: "And He will give their kings
748	into your hand." Exactly. You see, He promised something here, and indeed
749	it happened.
750	What does He say now? He says this: "The graven images of their gods
751	you shall burn with fire; you shall not covet the silver or gold upon them
752	and take it for yourself." Why? "Lest you be snared by it, for it is an abomination to
753	HaShem your Elokim." That is, you arrive and conquer
754	their village, and there is plunder. Part of what they had was
755	idols for idol worship. Now what would they do? The idol
756	might be made of wood or stone, but it was adorned with gold jewelry.
757	So He says: first of all, burn their idols.
758	But what about the silver and gold? Such a pity, there is silver and gold,
759	we could melt it down, maybe make rings
760	or bracelets for a woman, something. The Holy One, blessed be He, says: do not
761	covet the silver and gold upon them. What is on the idols you must also
762	burn and destroy. Why? "Lest you be snared by it," like a trap. Even
763	if you melt it down, it will always nag in your mind that this was once
764	idolatry, and perhaps in the end it will bring you down
765	and you will somehow serve it again. So He says "lest you be snared." You don't know.
766	You say, "No, I am strong." You cannot be
767	strong, you don't know. There was once an inclination
768	for idolatry. Just as a man is forbidden to be alone with
769	a woman who is not his wife, the prohibition called yichud,
770	you don't know. Do not say "I am strong." There is no
771	guardian for lions, the Sages say. You don't know
772	how it will bring you down. The same with idolatry. Even though
773	the Sages abolished the inclination for idolatry, we don't
774	understand this today, but once there was a very strong inclination
775	for idolatry. So He says you don't know
776	how it will bring you down, so
777	destroy it. Why? "For it is an abomination to
778	HaShem your Elokim."
779	"And you shall not bring an abomination into your house, lest you become a devoted thing like it.
780	You shall utterly detest it and utterly abhor it, for it is a devoted thing."
781	What does He say? Do not bring it into your house, and do not bring
782	anything connected to idolatry into the house. Where is this relevant
783	today? There are poor souls who don't know,
784	they come back from the East and bring statues of this Buddha,
785	what's his name? They bring statues of idol worship
786	like that. They put them in the house for decoration. All kinds of
787	things used for idol worship in the Far East, they put
788	these statues of this Buddha, and they think
789	it's decoration, but it is idolatry.
790	"Do not bring idolatry into your house." Now a person
791	will say: what's the problem? Do I bow to it? Do I
792	worship it? It's just decoration. Tell me, if now
793	the police come to someone's home, conduct a search, and find
794	there a machine for printing dollars,
795	and he says, "But I didn't print any dollars, I only
796	keep the machine," they will say, "Oh, fine, then you're
797	fine, you're great"? Of course not! Or a lab,
798	equipment for producing drugs, and he says, "But I didn't
799	produce drugs." But sir, you have prohibited equipment here.
800	So you see, even if you did not commit
801	the transgression, the very fact that you hold the tools for committing
802	the transgression, you will be held accountable for it in court. Right?
803	Same thing: why do you bring idolatry home? You
804	say, "But I didn't worship it." Then what is it doing in your
805	house? So whoever doesn't know, poor fellow, this is why
806	we listen to a Torah class. Each one should go through the house
807	and look whether he has anything resembling idolatry, all kinds
808	of statues, all kinds of unrelated things. Throw them out of
809	the house. Why do you need it? On the day of judgment
810	you will give an account for such a thing. May HaShem have mercy. Some
811	say "do not bring an abomination into your house" refers to the
812	beautiful woman, that if you go to war and see a beautiful
813	gentile woman, even though the Torah, under very
814	very very strict conditions, permitted her to you,
815	it says: do not bring the abomination into your house.
816	Now what else is "do not bring an abomination into your house,
817	and you will be a devoted thing like it"? Cherem has the letters of chomer, right,
818	without the vav, so that you not be far from HaShem, with a spirit,
819	with materialism without spirituality. For what is cherem? Cherem is
820	matter. Matter distances you from HaShem. Cherem is also
821	the letters of Ramach: if you bring the abomination, it will bring
822	troubles upon your two hundred forty-eight limbs. Cherem is also the letters of rachem,
823	for whoever repents and throws it out of
824	the house, HaShem has mercy on him. So you see how many
825	hints. Now what else does He say to him: "All the commandment which
826	I command you this day you shall observe to do, that you may live
827	and multiply and go in and possess the land which HaShem swore
828	to your fathers." That is, what does He say to him?
829	"That you may live and multiply." That is, see, the Torah
830	is a Torah of life, and the Holy One, blessed be He, promises
831	that keeping the mitzvot brings a person vitality. Wait, but
832	someone will say: wait, I know some who
833	keep nothing, and they live. I know one who transgresses
834	all the transgressions, eats pork, eats this,
835	desecrates Shabbat, and lives, right? He lives physically, like
836	a cow, like a dog; a dog lives too, a cow lives too. But
837	what? They live physically, but he has no spiritual
838	vitality. Vitality is a spiritual matter, and it continues
839	afterward to the World to Come. Woe to whoever comes
